question: In a 1500 m race, X beats Y by 100 m and X beats Z by 240 m. By what distance does Y beat Z in the same race?
solution:
**Given:**

In a 1500 m race, X beats Y by 100 m and X beats Z by 240 

**Calculation:**

When x goes 1500 m , y goes 1500-100 = 1400 m

When x goes 1500 m , z goes 1500-240 = 1260 m

When y goes 1400 m , z goes 1260 m

When y goes 1500 m , z goes,

⇒ (1260/1400) × 1500m = 1350 m

 Y beat Z in the same race by the distance of 1500 - 1350 = 150 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__** The race should be calculated as 1500m when calculating Y beat Z in the same race

**∴ The correct option is 3**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

 
• When X finishes 1500 m, Y has run 1400 m.
 
• When X finishes 1500 m, Z has run 1260 m.

Now, we need to find the distance by which Y beats Z in the same race.

When Y finishes 1500 m, the ratio of the distances run by Y and Z is the same as when X finishes. This is because the ratio of their speeds remains constant.

So, the ratio of distances run by Y and Z when X finishes the race is:

Distance run by Y: Distance run by Z=1400:1260

We can simplify this ratio by dividing both terms by their greatest common divisor (GCD), which is 20:

1400:1260 ​ =70:63

This means when Y runs 70 units of distance, Z runs 63 units of distance.

When Y runs the entire 1500 m race, we can set up a proportion to find the distance Z runs:

63/70​=Distance run by Z/1500​

Cross-multiplying gives:

70×Distance run by Z = 63×1500

70×Distance run by Z = 94500

Distance run by Z = 94500/70​

Distance run by Z = 1350 m

So, when Y finishes the 1500 m race, Z has run 1350 m.

Therefore, Y beats Z by:

1500 m − 1350 m = 150 m
